home.title: A clear monthly path from submission to recognition.
home.intro: Short and feature films are considered through an AI-assisted preliminary review, human finalist review, and dual approval before results are published online.

sections.title: One cycle every month
body: Entries close on the 20th at 23:59 JST. Results are scheduled for the last day of the month at 12:00 JST after review and approval.
items: Submission
Preliminary review
Human confirmation
Dual approval and publication

sections.title: Short and feature divisions
body: Films up to and including 35 minutes enter the short division. Films longer than 35 minutes enter the feature division.
items: Up to five candidates per division
Nine award categories per division
Digital certificates for confirmed winners

sections.title: Automation with accountable approval
body: AI supports intake checks, structured preliminary analysis, and administrative drafting. People review finalists and both operators must approve each proposed winner.
items: AI output is not a final award decision
Insufficient information is routed for human review
Publication and notification stop if either approval is missing

sections.title: Online results only at launch
body: No public venue screening is currently announced. Any future screening will be published only after a venue and operating details are confirmed.

about.title: A monthly recognition program built around a documented process.
about.intro: The program is being prepared for independent filmmakers who need a transparent submission route, a defined review calendar, and verifiable digital recognition.

sections.title: Purpose
body: We focus on clearly communicated rules, consistent monthly operations, and records that can be audited after each cycle.

sections.title: Operating principles
body: The site does not present an unconfirmed venue, jury, partner, history, or prior audience as fact.
items: Publish only verified information
Separate AI support from human authority
Retain approval and publication records
Correct errors through a traceable process

sections.title: How the program is operated
body: Two operators share finalist review and must both approve proposed awards. Administrative tasks are automated where they can be stopped, logged, and safely retried.

submit.title: Review the rules before opening the submission form.
submit.intro: Submissions will be accepted through a dedicated FilmFreeway listing. The live submission link and fee remain disabled until the organizer completes release settings.

sections.title: Before you submit
body: Confirm runtime, rights, subtitle availability, contact details, and the applicable fee and refund policy.
items: Short: 2,100 seconds or less
Feature: more than 2,100 seconds
The submitter must control the required exhibition and promotional rights
Non-English dialogue requires English subtitles

sections.title: Submission route
body: Use the FilmFreeway button on this page once it is enabled. We do not accept film files through the contact form or by ordinary email.

sections.title: Fee and refunds
body: The submission fee and final refund policy are required release inputs and are not yet published in preview mode.

sections.title: Monthly deadline
body: The monthly intake window runs from the 21st of the previous month through the 20th at 23:59 JST.

rules.title: Rules designed for consistent monthly review.
rules.intro: These rules are a working release draft. Organizer identity, fee, refund policy, and governing details must be approved before publication.

sections.title: Eligibility
body: Narrative, documentary, animation, experimental, and hybrid films may be submitted when the submitter has authority to enter the work.
items: A work may be submitted to one runtime division per cycle
Incomplete or inaccessible screeners may be ruled ineligible
False or materially misleading entry data may result in disqualification

sections.title: Runtime divisions
body: Runtime includes credits. Exactly 35:00 belongs to the short division; 35:01 and longer belongs to the feature division.

sections.title: Rights and permissions
body: The submitter is responsible for music, performance, archive, trademark, and other rights required for review and any authorized winner promotion.

sections.title: Language and subtitles
body: Films with dialogue not primarily in English must provide readable English subtitles unless the work is intentionally non-verbal.

sections.title: AI-assisted preliminary review
body: AI may support metadata validation, structured preliminary analysis, and administrative processing. Finalists are reviewed by people and awards require two-person approval.

sections.title: Fees and refunds
body: The approved fee and refund terms will be inserted before release. No fee should be paid while this page remains marked as a preview.

sections.title: Withdrawal and corrections
body: Requests must include the FilmFreeway submission identifier and come from the registered contact address. Withdrawal does not automatically create a refund right.

selection.title: A monthly review sequence with explicit stopping points.
selection.intro: Each stage produces a record. Missing data, approval failures, or publication failures stop the workflow instead of silently moving forward.

sections.title: 1. Intake and eligibility
body: Submission data is imported from a monthly FilmFreeway CSV. Runtime, access, required metadata, and duplicate identifiers are checked before review.

sections.title: 2. AI-assisted preliminary analysis
body: AI returns structured criteria, evidence references, risk flags, and confidence. It may recommend candidates but cannot confirm a finalist or winner.

sections.title: 3. Human finalist review
body: Up to five candidates per division are divided between two operators for first viewing. Any proposed winner must then be reviewed by both operators.

sections.title: 4. Dual approval
body: Each proposed award requires two recorded approvals. Missing, conflicting, or revoked approval blocks generation, publication, and notification.

sections.title: 5. Publication and notification
body: After the site publication succeeds, certificate and winner notifications may be sent. Re-running a completed stage must not duplicate a message or certificate.

awards.title: Nine categories in each runtime division.
awards.intro: Short and feature divisions use the same award structure. A film may receive more than one award when both operators approve the result.

sections.title: Award categories
body: The canonical category list is shared by the English and Japanese sites and by certificate generation.

sections.title: Allocation rule
body: When a division has at least one eligible submission, one winner is selected for each category. Only a division with zero eligible submissions is marked no award.
items: One work may receive multiple awards
Awards are not final until both approvals are recorded
Corrections create a new certificate version and preserve the audit trail

sections.title: Digital certificate
body: Confirmed winners receive a PDF certificate with a unique certificate identifier that can be checked on the verification page.

sections.title: Official laurels
body: Confirmed winners receive an editable SVG laurel and a transparent PNG export.

winners.title: Monthly results will appear here after dual approval.
winners.intro: No winners are shown in preview mode. A cycle is added only after publication succeeds and notification records are linked to the release.

sections.title: Latest cycle
body: There is no published cycle yet.

sections.title: Monthly archive
body: Published cycles will be listed by month with certificate verification links.

sections.title: Film stills and credits
body: Winner pages use only approved credits and stills for which publication permission is recorded.

faq.title: Answers about submission, review, and results.
faq.intro: If an answer depends on an unpublished fee, venue, or account setting, the site says so instead of filling the gap.

sections.title: Is this an in-person festival?
body: At launch, results are published online and no public venue screening is announced.

sections.title: Does AI decide the winners?
body: No. AI supports preliminary analysis and administration. People review finalists and both operators must approve proposed winners.

sections.title: Which division applies at exactly 35 minutes?
body: A runtime of 35:00 belongs to the short division. Any runtime above 35:00 belongs to the feature division.

sections.title: Can one film receive multiple awards?
body: Yes. Multiple awards are allowed when each result receives the required approvals.

sections.title: When are results published?
body: The target is 12:00 JST on the last day of the month, subject to successful review, approval, and publication checks.

sections.title: How are certificates verified?
body: Use the unique certificate identifier on the verification page. The public record does not expose private submission data.

sections.title: What is the refund policy?
body: The final policy is a required release input and is not published while this site is in preview mode.

contact.title: Send an operational question with the relevant identifier.
contact.intro: Do not send screeners, passwords, identity documents, payment card data, or other unnecessary sensitive information through this form.

sections.title: What to include
body: Include your name, email, topic, message, and FilmFreeway submission identifier when the inquiry concerns an entry.

sections.title: Response process
body: The form sends an automated receipt only after server-side anti-bot verification. Individual replies are prepared in scheduled operating windows and may require human review.

sections.title: Privacy
body: Inquiry data is stored in the private operations system and used only to handle the request, maintain an audit record, and meet legal obligations.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice remains a draft until the organizer identity, location, retention schedule, and processor settings are approved.

sections.title: Information collected
body: Submission records, inquiry details, correspondence identifiers, review records, award records, and technical anti-abuse data may be processed.

sections.title: Purpose of use
body: Data is used to administer submissions, answer inquiries, conduct and audit review, publish approved results, issue certificates, prevent abuse, and meet legal obligations.

sections.title: Retention
body: A final retention schedule will be published before release. Data must not be retained longer than the approved operational or legal purpose requires.

sections.title: Service providers
body: The final notice will identify applicable submission, Google Workspace, anti-bot, hosting, and AI processing services after accounts and regions are configured.

sections.title: Questions and requests
body: Use the contact route for applicable access, correction, deletion, or objection requests. Identity may need to be verified before a request is completed.

terms.title: Website and participation terms
terms.intro: These terms are not ready for production until organizer, fee, refund, governing-law, and signature details are approved.

sections.title: Website use
body: Users must not interfere with the site, attempt unauthorized access, submit malicious content, or misrepresent affiliation with the program.

sections.title: Submissions
body: Film entries are governed by the published rules and the confirmed FilmFreeway listing. The submitter is responsible for accurate data and required rights.

sections.title: Decisions and corrections
body: Published decisions are produced through the stated approval process. Clerical or factual errors may be corrected with a preserved audit record.

sections.title: Fees and refunds
body: The approved fee and refund policy will be inserted before release.

sections.title: Liability and governing terms
body: The final limitation, governing-law, and dispute provisions require organizer review and must not be inferred from this preview.

accessibility.title: A site designed for keyboard, screen reader, and zoom use.
accessibility.intro: Accessibility is checked before each release and issues are recorded for correction.

sections.title: Commitment
body: We aim to keep content perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust across modern devices and assistive technologies.

sections.title: Measures
body: Semantic headings, keyboard-visible focus, text alternatives, contrast checks, responsive layouts, reduced-motion support, and form error messages are included in release checks.

sections.title: Report a barrier
body: Use the contact form and select accessibility. Describe the page, task, device, browser, and assistive technology when possible.

verify.title: Check a published certificate identifier.
verify.intro: Verification confirms only the public award record associated with the identifier. It does not expose submission or review data.

sections.title: Enter the certificate ID
body: Use the exact identifier printed on the PDF certificate.

sections.title: Verification result
body: A confirmed record displays the cycle, division, award, film title, credited recipient, issue date, and current certificate status.
